H1.note: mechanism: variants that disrupt the TREM2/PLCG2/ABI3 complex drive AD, so each gene is protective. The chain is three fragments (TREM2 -> PLCG2 -> AD; ABI3 ~ TREM2; ABI3 -> AD); the title's 'complex' is not a step

H2.note: mechanism: APOE binding stimulates TREM2 signalling, 'protecting the brain against Alzheimer's disease progression', so both claims are neg on progression. No step says progression: H2.2 (shared with H4.2, whose mechanism says risk) and H2.3 read as risk, so neither claim has a route. APOE reaches TREM2 only by an unsigned 'binds' step

H3.note: mechanism: INPP5D represses RIPK1, a neuroprotective brake on AD. The chain never links RIPK1 to AD; the bridge S11 comes from a 'suggest' sentence in the run's own citation and carries no weight

H4.note: mechanism: MS4A4A inhibits TREM2 activity and so 'increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease'

findings.detail: No gene-to-AD effect step has a citation of its own that states it: the run cites an Open Targets score (undirected) plus a variant association or a variant knock-in, so S4, S6 and S9 have empty evidence and S2 (PLCG2) keeps only a review moved from H1.1.

Nothing cited states that TREM2 activates PLCG2: the review only lists both as GWAS genes and STRING has no experimental channel; the nearest text, 'P522R PLCG2 coding variant (rs72824905) is downstream of TREM2' (PMID:42357928, cited at H1.2), gives order but no sign.

The run reads each gene's direction from its variants (PLCG2 P522R protective, ABI3 S209F risk, TREM2 R62H risk, PMID:28714976) without any cited text saying which variants are gain or loss of function, which is what the gene-level sign needs.

H1.2 ends at Alzheimer disease and H1.3 starts again at ABI3; the chain is three fragments (TREM2 -> PLCG2 -> AD, ABI3 ~ TREM2, ABI3 -> AD), so ABI3 never joins the TREM2-PLCG2 axis the title calls a complex.
The title's 'signaling complex' rests on ABI3 ~ TREM2, whose only support is a STRING text-mining edge (0.63; experimental and database 0); PMID:28714976 reports the two genes' variants separately.

H3.1 ends at RIPK1 and H3.2 starts again at INPP5D; no step takes RIPK1 to AD, the link the mechanism depends on. The only text for it is a 'suggest' sentence about LOAD in PMID:41633359 (bridge S11, kind hypothesis).

PMID:41633359's in vivo INPP5D-deficiency phenotypes are neuronal TDP-43 pathology, neuron loss and motor dysfunction (framed as AD-ALS comorbidity), not AD; the run cites them for 'INPP5D inhibits Alzheimer disease'.
H2's mechanism and falsification say APOE binding activates TREM2, but the step is 'binds' with unknown polarity and H2.3 is an unsigned association, so APOE has no signed route to AD (no route).

H2 says APOE signalling through TREM2 protects against AD, while its only directional APOE citation (PMID:8346443) says APOE epsilon 4 allele dose raises AD risk; the run never says which APOE allele or level is the protective ligand.

Every subject and object has an empty CURIE except MONDO:0004975; RIPK1 is typed 'other' not 'gene'; and the context cell type 'mature microglial cell' is left ungrounded though it is exactly CL:0002629's label.

Every one of the 11 steps, including the six that end at Alzheimer disease, carries the same context 'mature microglial cell'; a disease cannot be restricted to a cell type, so the context was read as a blanket default and dropped rather than refining every node.

supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence are empty for all four hypotheses; every citation is a chain citation, and the budget's min_evidence_per_hypothesis 2 is met by counting OT and STRING records.

Three steps restate the titles of 2026 primary papers (INPP5D -| RIPK1, MS4A4A -| TREM2, PLCG2 protects), and they are the only steps a primary paper names end to end, though the PLCG2 title summarises a P522R variant knock-in; the steps the agent composed itself (TREM2 -> PLCG2, gene -> AD) have no stating citation.

PMID:42357928's 'Alzheimer's Protection by PLCγ2' comes from a P522R knock-in in amyloidosis mice where total amyloid burden was unaffected; the protection is plaque compaction and synapse sparing, and the evidence is about a variant, not PLCG2 dosage.

H1's falsification knocks out PLCG2 in microglial cell cultures but names Alzheimer disease as the readout, which a culture cannot show; it also places ABI3 downstream of TREM2, while the chain has ABI3 as the subject of its TREM2 association.

The abstention for RNPS1 and LPIN2 cites OT:RNPS1-MONDO_0004975, PMID:41205924 and PMID:21283692, none of which is in sources.json, so its claims ('no genetic association for LPIN2') cannot be checked.
The format has no place for a run's abstention (genes covered, reason, evidence), and sources.json does not fetch abstention citations, so abstentions go uncurated.

The guide says to refine when 'the step's context limits the result', but gives no rule for a run that stamps one cell-type context on every step, gene-to-disease steps included; I dropped it, refining would have produced 'Alzheimer disease in microglia'.

BioLean cannot relate a variant's direction to its gene's effect sign (no gain/loss-of-function qualifier on a variant), so variant GWAS rows and variant knock-ins can never support a gene-level effect step; a title that names the gene ('Alzheimer's Protection by PLCγ2') for a variant knock-in is the hard case, and the guide does not say whether the title or the design decides.
A gene-gene 'associated_with' step (ABI3 ~ TREM2, network co-membership) has no natural target: assoc needs amount or activity, and I chose activity arbitrarily.

The evidence-kind table has no row for an Open Targets association score kept for an unsigned association (it lists OT only as a no_direction exclusion); curations so far use observational, curatedDb and textMined for it, which weigh 1/2, 4/5 and 3/10. Here: observational.

PMID:41435829's one span pools macrophages, microglia, non-human primates and a mouse model; an evidence row takes one kind and one taxon, and the taxon list has no primate, so I recorded mechanistic, mouse.
PMID:41633359's abstract does not name the species of its INPP5D-RIPK1 interaction work; omitting taxon means human by default, and there is no 'unknown' taxon.

H2's mechanism says 'progression' but its chain says 'inhibits Alzheimer disease'; the guide takes the claim's sign from the title or mechanism and its target from the chain, but does not say where the aspect comes from when they disagree (the audit used the mechanism's progression, leaving H2 without a route; curations of other runs split both ways).
The PLCG2 arm has belief 3/5 (one review) and gets the same verdict, 'unsupported', as the arms with belief 0; a label for 'some support, below 0.8' would keep the two apart in the report.

H1's title says the complex 'clears amyloid plaques', but its own citations say the protective PLCG2 R522 knock-in left 'total amyloid burden ... unaffected' (it compacts plaques; PMID:42357928) and the ABI3 risk-variant knock-in lowered dense-core burden 'without affecting diffuse or total Aβ' (PMID:42092345).

H2's mechanism claims APOE-TREM2 signalling protects against Alzheimer's disease progression, but no step or citation is about progression: H2.2 is the same 'TREM2 inhibits AD' step as H4.2 (whose mechanism says risk) and PMID:8346443 is about risk and onset, so H2 has no route.

an Open Targets association score is computed from genetic-association and literature evidence, not a curated assertion (curatedDb is UniProt text, Reactome, ChEMBL); observational is the kind most other curations use for a kept OT score, and curatedDb's 4/5 alone lifted S7 to 'established'

the claim's aspect comes from what the hypothesis asserts: H2's mechanism says 'protecting the brain against Alzheimer's disease progression' and the title names no aspect; the chain's 'inhibits Alzheimer disease' has no aspect word and was read as risk by default, so the mismatch is a result (no route), not a reason to change the claim
